findings.title: Test cleanup removes literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDPs, leaking test data and failing cleanup
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup registrations use `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` with the hard-coded string "alias" instead of the actual aliases that were created ("idp-alias-" + i at line 381, and "idp-alias-20" at line 425). None of the 20+ identity providers created by the test are ever removed, so they leak into subsequent tests in the realm (any test that counts or lists realm IDPs will see stale brokers). Additionally, at cleanup time the registered runnable calls remove() on the non-existent "alias" resource, which returns 404 and can make the cleanup itself fail. The correct call is `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove)` (and `get("idp-alias-20")` for the later one). Note the same copy-pasted defect exists at line 303 in testCacheIDPByOrg, which suggests the bug was copied from there.

findings.title: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate evaluates the login predicate on the organization-wrapped model, so invalidation can be wrongly skipped
findings.body: In update(), the "original" model passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate comes from getById(), which returns a model wrapped by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. That wrapper overrides isEnabled() to return false whenever the linked organization (or the organization provider) is disabled, regardless of the IDP's own enabled flag. The login caches, however, are populated purely from intrinsic IDP properties (enabled, linkOnly, hideOnLogin, brokerPublic, organizationId) — an IDP belonging to a disabled org is still stored in the cached login lists. Scenario: (1) an org-linked, public, enabled IDP is cached in the login list; (2) the organization is disabled (this does not touch the IDP, so no cache invalidation); (3) an admin updates the IDP to disabled or non-public — the wrapped original fails getLoginPredicate() (isEnabled()=false due to the disabled org) and the updated model also fails, so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns early and the login caches are NOT invalidated even though the IDP is in them and no longer qualifies; (4) when the org is re-enabled, getForLogin serves the stale cached list containing an IDP that is disabled/non-public, violating the SPI contract that getForLogin returns only IDPs available for login. The impact on the login page is currently masked because OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean re-filters, but any other consumer of getForLogin gets stale results. Fix: compute the predicate on the raw delegate model (e.g. idpDelegate.getById(...)) instead of the wrapped one, so the skip-invalidation decision depends only on intrinsic IDP properties.
